note: ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO FIXTURE prepared by the Field Verse SE team. NOT ML predictions or agronomic recommendations. Indicator ratings are illustrative 1–5 values chosen by people from general crop knowledge.
limitations: Demo strategies were prepared by hand for a typical rain-fed soybean farm near Sorriso; they are not calculated for your exact field.
No market prices, logistics or input costs were used.
Soil values come from a global estimate (SoilGrids), not a soil test of your field.

strategies.name: Soybean – Second-crop maize (current)
strategies.summary: Soybean in the main wet season, then maize planted right after harvest to use the last rains.

reasons: This double-crop pattern is widely used in the region.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: Both crops are rain-fed; maize needs moisture late in the season.

indicators.label: Soil cover through the year
indicators.explanation: Field is bare in the dry season (July–September).

indicators.label: Exposure to dry spells
indicators.explanation: Second-crop maize is exposed if the rains stop early.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: Two commodities. No price data was used.

notes: NASA POWER shows rain falls sharply from about 112 mm in April to about 30 mm in May, so late maize is exposed.
Bare during the dry season unless residues are kept.

benefits.text: Two harvests from the same land each year.
Soybean is a legume and may leave some nitrogen for the maize.

risks.text: If soybean is planted late, the maize grows into the dry season and yields can drop.
Repeated soybean can build up soybean pests and diseases.

explanation.summary: This is your current pattern, shown as the starting point for comparison.
details: Rainfall data shows a long wet season, then almost no rain from May to September.
explanation.technical: Baseline strategy. Indicator ratings are illustrative demo values.

dataGaps.text: Your actual soybean planting and harvest dates.
No soil test of your field is available.

localChecks: Check the agricultural zoning calendar (planting windows) for your municipality.

uncertainty.notes: Illustrative demo content; no model has evaluated this field.

strategies.name: Soybean – Second-crop sorghum
strategies.summary: Soybean in the main season, then sorghum, which copes better if the rains end early.

reasons: Sorghum is often discussed as a second crop when planting is late.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: Sorghum generally needs less water than maize.

indicators.label: Exposure to dry spells
indicators.explanation: Sorghum tolerates heat and dry spells better than maize.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: Sorghum markets can be smaller than maize. No price data used.

notes: Better matched to the falling rainfall in April–May (NASA POWER).

benefits.text: Lower risk when the rains finish early.
Allows a slightly later second-crop planting than maize.

risks.text: Sorghum markets and prices may be less attractive than maize locally.
Birds can damage sorghum grain heads.

explanation.summary: This option lowers dry-season risk for the second crop by choosing a more drought-tolerant grain.
details: Rainfall data shows a steep drop after April, which is when the second crop is filling grain.
explanation.technical: Illustrative demo strategy. Indicator ratings are hand-prepared, not model outputs.

localChecks: Talk with local buyers or cooperatives about sorghum demand.

strategies.name: Soybean – Sunn hemp cover
strategies.summary: Soybean in the main season, then a sunn hemp cover crop to protect and build the soil.

steps.notes: Cover-crop residue left on the surface.

reasons: Sunn hemp is a fast cover crop that can use the late wet-season rains.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: A short cover crop in the wet months.

indicators.label: Soil cover through the year
indicators.explanation: Residue can protect soil into the dry season.

indicators.label: Exposure to dry spells
indicators.explanation: No second cash crop at risk from early dry season.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: Gives up the second harvest. No price data used.

notes: Uses February–April rains (about 110–260 mm per month, NASA POWER).
Residue cover through much of the dry season.

benefits.text: Builds soil organic matter and protects soil from erosion.
Some farmers use sunn hemp to help manage certain soil pests (nematodes) — verify locally.
Lower cash risk than a late second crop.

risks.text: No second harvest to sell this year.
Cover-crop seed and sowing add cost.

explanation.summary: This option trades the second harvest for longer-term soil benefits.
details: Useful in years when soybean is harvested too late for a safe second crop.
explanation.technical: Illustrative demo strategy. Indicator ratings are hand-prepared, not model outputs.

dataGaps.text: Whether the soil benefit pays back the lost second harvest on your farm.
Sunn hemp seed price and availability.

localChecks: Ask a local agronomist whether a cover-crop year suits your soil and pest situation.

uncertainty.notes: Illustrative demo content; soil benefits build over several years.
